title: Butternut Squash and Sage Blini
changes_from_base: Yeast-free: roasted butternut purée, buttermilk and sage-infused olive oil go into a quick batter of wholemeal, buckwheat and plain flour raised with baking powder and bicarbonate; cooked as small 5-7 cm blini.
summary: Nutty buckwheat pancakes infused with roasted squash purée and finished with crispy sage leaves, best served with soured cream.
equipment: griddle or large non-stick frying pan

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Roast Squash
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 200 °C (180 °C fan), line a baking tray with foil and oil lightly; lay 450 g butternut squash (seeded, cut side down, skin up) on the tray and roast 45-60 minutes until completely soft.

steps.title: Purée
steps.text: Cool, scoop the flesh from the skin and purée in a food processor until you have about 180 g.

steps.title: Dry Mix
steps.text: Sift 70 g wholemeal flour, 70 g buckwheat flour, 70 g plain flour, 2 tsp baking powder, 1 tsp bicarbonate of soda, 1 tsp caster sugar and ½ tsp fine salt together into a bowl.

steps.title: Wet Mix
steps.text: Beat 2 large eggs in a medium bowl, whisk in 360 ml buttermilk and the 180 g squash purée, then mix in 2 tbsp oil.

steps.title: Sage Oil
steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a small frying pan over medium-high heat, fry 1 tbsp sage leaves about 10 seconds until starting to crisp, remove from the heat and cool, then add both oil and sage to the wet mixture.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Whisk the flour mixture quickly into the wet ingredients.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Heat a griddle over medium-high, oil lightly and drop 1-2 tbsp batter per blini (5-7 cm across); cook each batch until bubbles break through, flip and cook until lightly browned, keeping finished blini warm under a clean cloth.

tips: Roast the squash fully until completely tender so it purées into a smooth paste
Fry the sage briefly until just crisp to avoid bitterness from overcooking
Keep cooked blini warm under a cloth so all are ready to serve at the same time
storage: Serve whilst warm. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
